works.name: ABISS: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Systems Through Agent Interaction
works.summary: Builds taxonomy-conditioned questions and evaluates SQL agents through multi-turn conversations with style-aware simulated users. Its model-council validation approximates unanswerability rather than proving it, and the controlled simulator does not establish performance with real users.

works.name: AmbiSQL: Interactive Ambiguity Detection and Resolution for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Detects ambiguous phrases, presents multiple-choice clarification options, and rewrites the question before passing it to a SQL generator. The demonstration integrates XiYan-SQL and a small set of ambiguous examples, so its interface and detection mechanisms should be separated from claims of general end-to-end reliability.

works.name: An OMOP-Based Open-Source Text-to-SQL Benchmark Dataset
works.summary: Evaluates SQL generation or explicit abstention over synthetic OMOP data using concept-normalized questions and EHRSQL-derived templates and unanswerables. Execution and penalty-based reliability scores test the specified SQL-or-refuse contract; raw-text entity linking, ambiguous concept resolution and clinical deployment safety remain outside the demonstrated evaluation.

works.name: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation
works.summary: Introduces structured selection among ambiguity points and interpretations, with a corpus built over real-world databases. The benchmark separates disambiguation from SQL generation and uses a user simulator, so its reported results remain specific to the annotated alternatives and interaction protocol.

works.name: AtomSQL: Interactive Disambiguation of NL-to-SQL via User-Guided Atom-Level Alignment
works.summary: Exposes disagreements between SQL candidates as clause-level atoms aligned with phrases in the question, then uses user selections to adjust future preferences. The demonstration makes alternative interpretations inspectable, but resolution is limited to candidates supplied by the active models: users must reformulate when none expresses their intent.

works.name: Beyond Correctness: Resolving Underspecification in Agentic Text-to-SQL
works.summary: PlanPool stores clarification questions in an explicit mutable pool, requiring each planned question to be asked or deliberately dropped before SQL submission. Experiments on BIRD-Interact- and Spider-derived tasks distinguish ambiguity coverage from execution correctness, but do not guarantee that the initial pool captures every missing constraint.

works.name: BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation for Large Language Models via Lens of Dynamic Interactions
works.summary: Combines database documentation, hierarchical business knowledge, executable tests, and a function-driven user simulator to evaluate conversational and autonomous agent interaction across ambiguous CRUD tasks. Its Full and Lite tasks measure success within a specified simulator and action budget; they do not establish that an assistant has resolved every real user's intent.

works.name: Bounded Semantic Planning and Deterministic Compilation for Reliable Enterprise Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Separates multi-turn semantic planning over governed options from deterministic SQL compilation and checks, targeting wrong relationship roles and aggregation grain. Its insurance-benchmark comparison uses a small adjudicated set and gives the planner semantic artifacts unavailable to the DDL baseline, so it does not isolate compilation as the cause of the gain.

works.name: Building SQL Equivalence Proofs from Query Rewrite Rules
works.summary: EquiTrace constructs replayable SQL-equivalence derivations by aligning query plans and composing admitted rewrite rules under schema constraints. Proof validity depends on those rules and applicability conditions; unsuccessful bounded search returns UNKNOWN, not inequivalence. This supports semantic evaluation of candidate/reference SQL pairs without establishing that the reference captures the user’s intent.

works.name: Certified Against Which Oracle? Execution Labels Set the Reported Risk of Conformal Abstention for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Audits conformal abstention by changing the database-based oracle used to cluster SQL candidates and label correctness, then comparing with expert judgments. The study shows why reported risk must be interpreted relative to the oracle and benchmark quality, rather than treated as an unconditional semantic guarantee.

works.name: CLARITY: A Framework and Benchmark for Conversational Language Ambiguity and Unanswerability in Interactive NL2SQL Systems
works.summary: Generates questions with interacting ambiguity or unanswerability sources, schema-grounded diagnostic metadata, and helpful, partial or unhelpful conversational continuations. Spider and BIRD experiments test detection, localization and resolution under these constructed settings; they do not establish live-user or production performance.

works.name: Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL in Large Language Models
works.summary: Studies black-box consistency signals and white-box SQL-aware confidence estimates, including execution-based grounding. The work estimates reliability without gold answers at inference time; a confidence score alone does not determine whether the user's request is ambiguous or unsupported.

works.name: Developing and Benchmarking Verification Algorithms to Improve Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: Compares Round-Trip Critique and Synthetic Execution Consistency for checking candidate SQL against natural-language requests without gold labels at inference time. The study connects verification to benchmark auditing and selective abstention, while false acceptance/rejection trade-offs, generator-dependent error examples and imperfect ordering labels limit conclusions about general semantic correctness.

works.name: Disentangling Ambiguity from Instability in Large Language Models: A Clinical Text-to-SQL Case Study
works.summary: CLUES builds a graph over interpretations and answers to separate variation caused by question ambiguity from variation within the same interpretation. This decomposition supports different clarification and review routes, while its clinical case-study results and domain-dependent thresholds should not be treated as validated clinical deployment guarantees.

works.name: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents
works.summary: Evaluates source discovery, cross-database coordination and execution, including tasks with alternative source interpretations. Its controlled Ask-Once protocol reveals a branch-specific answer only when a question targets the intended semantic slot, so clarification gains are bounded to the simulator and its question-alignment judge.

works.name: EntSQL: A Benchmark for Grounding Text-to-SQL in Long-Context Enterprise Knowledge
works.summary: Pairs Chinese and English enterprise questions with business documents to test whether models can ground SQL in internal metric definitions, reporting conventions, and organizational rules. It isolates missing business context as an important failure source, but does not directly evaluate a clarify-or-abstain interaction policy.

works.name: Evaluating LLMs on Conversational Text-to-SQL under Chain Ambiguity and Intent Drift
works.summary: Introduces TIDE-Bench with dependent clarification chains and user revisions that retract earlier commitments, plus metrics for recognizing and resolving those changes. The 1,542 samples derive from 514 BIRD anchor queries, and the linked repository was only a placeholder when checked despite the manuscript's release statement.

works.name: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
works.summary: Uses SQL reserved-word seeding, persona prompts, ambiguity handling, and alignment filtering to generate complex NL-SQL training pairs with compact models. Its human checks and downstream training experiments support the tested data pipeline, rather than establishing that automatically generated interpretations exhaust real user intent.

works.name: LatentRefusal: Latent-Signal Refusal for Unanswerable Text-to-SQL Queries
works.summary: Predicts answerability from intermediate LLM activations using a lightweight Tri-Residual Gated Encoder before SQL generation. The approach requires access to hidden states and supervised probing; its classification performance does not establish that all admitted SQL answers are correct.

works.name: Never the Number: Structural Abstention for AI Systems Whose Answers Are Consumed as Fact
works.summary: Proposes separating generative interpretation from a deterministic query kernel, using user confirmation and a bounded set of supported question forms to decline requests outside that set. The technical report describes an architectural pattern and case study; its primary record explicitly states that code, schemas, datasets and performance metrics are not included.

works.name: ODUTQA-MDC: A Task for Open-Domain Underspecified Tabular QA with Multi-turn Dialogue-based Clarification
works.summary: Combines an underspecified tabular-QA dataset with simulated dialogue clarification and the MAIC-TQA multi-agent framework for retrieval, interpretation, and answer refinement. Its SQL-generation component makes it relevant to database agents, but the benchmark's primary task is open-domain tabular QA rather than conventional schema-conditioned text-to-SQL.

works.name: Pervasive Annotation Errors Break Text-to-SQL Benchmarks and Leaderboards
works.summary: Audits annotations in BIRD and Spider 2.0-Snow and re-evaluates agents on a corrected BIRD subset, showing that reference errors can change reported rankings. This supports checking evaluation labels before interpreting reliability scores; the findings concern the inspected benchmark versions and subsets, not every current leaderboard.

works.name: PleaSQLarify: Visual Pragmatic Repair for Natural Language Database Querying
works.summary: Organizes clarification around interpretable decision variables and exposes alternative actions and belief updates in a visual interface. A study with twelve participants supports the interaction design, while broader end-to-end reliability remains a separate evaluation question.

works.name: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems
works.summary: Pairs flawed requests with valid originals to evaluate premise detection, error-type identification and SQL abstention under three prompting settings. Stronger critique instructions can also reject valid questions, and the static response evaluation does not establish live clarification ability.

works.name: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL
works.summary: AIR uses competing agents to propose interpretations, prunes SQL candidates by differences in executed results, and synthesizes contrastive clarification questions. Schema-only describes the generation context: verification still accesses the full database, and agreement on the current data does not prove semantic equivalence. Its AMBROSIA/AmbiQT evaluation measures interpretation coverage rather than live-user clarification outcomes.

works.name: QDA-SQL: Questions Enhanced Dialogue Augmentation for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Generates multi-turn dialogues with varied question types and applies validation and correction before using them for text-to-SQL training. It targets ambiguous and unanswerable requests, but synthetic-data filtering and reported downstream gains do not by themselves validate every generated conversation.

works.name: RAQS-SQL: Schema and Value Ambiguity Resolution in Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Combines question-to-column alignment with semantic and hierarchical value matching, and introduces AmbiVal from Spider and BIRD. The approach focuses on schema and value ambiguity; those grounding tasks should be distinguished from evaluating a full clarification dialogue.

works.name: Reasoning about Intent for Ambiguous Requests
works.summary: IntentRL trains models to emit interpretation-answer pairs, rewarding coverage for ambiguous inputs and precision for unambiguous ones using answer supervision. It evaluates conversational QA and text-to-SQL, including AMBROSIA and AmbiQT, but its principal output enumerates alternatives in one response rather than resolving intent through live dialogue.

works.name: Reliable End-to-End Text-to-SQL Generation
works.summary: RTS++ combines execution-based uncertainty with conformal calibration to decide when to abstain or seek human feedback during SQL generation. Its reliability claims depend on the calibration assumptions, correctness labels, and tested database setting; they do not prove the user's intent has been fully specified.

works.name: Rethinking Text-to-SQL: Dynamic Multi-turn SQL Interaction for Real-world Database Exploration
works.summary: DySQL-Bench evaluates evolving requests through an interacting simulated user, SQL agent, and executable database, including operations that alter state. Its 1,072 tasks across 13 domains stress continued intent tracking and repeated-run reliability, while success remains conditional on the benchmark's generated tasks and simulator.

works.name: ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL
works.summary: Uses a Prover-Refuter cascade to judge candidate SQL against the question, with the reference query used as challenge evidence, and validates judgments on ROSE-VEC expert-consensus cases. Agreement on those selected cases does not prove semantic correctness for all interpretations or remove dependence on the chosen judges and acceptance criteria.

works.name: RTS-SQL
works.summary: Uses candidate execution-result agreement and execution entropy to support SQL selection and abstention.

works.name: Same SQL, Different Decision: Aggregate Risk Hides Cross-Lingual Instability in Text-to-SQL Verification
works.summary: Holds candidate SQL, schema and execution labels fixed while varying question language to audit execute-or-defer decisions. Similar aggregate risk can hide different queries being executed; the study tests score adjustment and translation to English. Results concern English-generated SQL and two main verifiers, with execution-match labels and imperfect translation limiting semantic and end-to-end claims.

works.name: SCARE: A Benchmark for SQL Correction and Question Answerability Classification for Reliable EHR Question Answering
works.summary: Tests a post-hoc component that classifies questions as answerable, ambiguous or unanswerable while verifying or correcting candidate SQL. Its question–candidate-SQL triples span three EHR databases and expose a classification-versus-correction trade-off, without validating clinical safety.

works.name: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs
works.summary: Builds a graph of schema relationships and business entities from query logs, then retrieves context for SQL generation in poorly documented databases. Its BEAVER experiment instead builds edges from schema metadata, so it does not independently test log-based discovery. Executability and judge preferences do not establish complete intent resolution or abstention ability.

works.name: SOMA-SQL: Resolving Multi-Source Ambiguity in NL-to-SQL via Synthetic Log and Execution Probing
works.summary: Creates synthetic query logs and executes targeted probes to gather evidence for SQL selection and repair under ambiguous schemas or questions. Autonomous database inspection can reduce grounding uncertainty, but does not directly reveal preferences or facts known only to the user.

works.name: SpotIt+
works.summary: Searches for database counterexamples to candidate/reference SQL equivalence using bounded verification and database constraints.

works.name: SpotIt+: Verification-based Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Database Constraints
works.summary: Adds database-constraint mining to bounded SQL equivalence checking so distinguishing examples better reflect plausible data. Constraint extraction is best effort, and verification still concerns a generated/reference query pair under the chosen bounds and assumptions.

works.name: SpotIt: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Formal Verification
works.summary: Uses bounded formal verification to search for database instances that distinguish generated SQL from a reference query. Counterexamples expose differences missed by ordinary execution tests; an equivalence result is limited to supported SQL semantics and the specified bound.

works.name: TACO: A Benchmark for Open-Domain Text-to-SQL with Ambiguous and Cross-Database Queries
works.summary: Tests vague questions, unknown target databases, and queries spanning heterogeneous databases; TACO-SQL combines rewriting, table linking, and planning. The benchmark primarily scores executable SQL against selected references, so its open-domain ambiguity challenge differs from enumerating all interpretations or measuring clarification quality.

works.name: TraceSQL: Traceable Answerability Estimation for Reference-Free Text-to-SQL Verification
works.summary: Learns a verifier from 67 diagnostic features describing ambiguity, question requirements, schema-SQL consistency, SQL structure, and intent alignment. Its answerability estimate concerns whether a candidate SQL answers a question and is evaluated on generated BIRD queries; it is not a general proof that the underlying request is answerable.

works.name: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents
works.summary: Adds a classifier-based confidence layer that can reject a question before execution, stop a failing trajectory or withhold the final answer. EHRSQL results show a coverage–reliability–computation trade-off under configurable penalties, with strong penalties leading to substantial abstention.

works.name: What Is a Clarification? Estimating Model-Dependent Input Ambiguity
works.summary: Distinguishes interpretations admitted by an input from answers accessible to a particular model and estimates answer sets through answer–clarification–answer consistency. Experiments include executable Text-to-SQL, while the abstract's decision-policy results for answering, clarifying, and abstaining are reported for question answering.

works.name: What Predicts Correctness in Text-to-SQL? A Selective-Prediction Study
works.summary: Compares self-consistency, model scores, and reasoning-based verification signals for ranking SQL correctness and selecting which questions to answer. Results cover the studied BIRD and Spider configurations and highlight that verifier performance within known schemas need not transfer to unseen schemas.

works.name: CLEAR: A Parser-Independent Disambiguation Framework for NL2SQL
works.summary: Builds candidate schema mappings, collects multiple-choice selections and rewrites both question and schema for a downstream parser. CLAMBSQL adds ambiguity and clarification annotations, so the evaluation depends on those annotated choices rather than unconstrained conversations.

works.name: Confidence Estimation for Error Detection in Text-to-SQL Systems
works.summary: Studies entropy-based selective classification and calibration for deciding when to withhold SQL under distribution shifts and unanswerable requests. Its error-detection results distinguish irrelevant questions from incorrect generations, so improved rejection should not be interpreted as solving all semantic errors.

works.name: Disambiguate First, Parse Later: Generating Interpretations for Ambiguity Resolution in Semantic Parsing
works.summary: Generates initial natural-language readings and trains an infilling model to recover interpretations that the initial LLM omits, then parses each reading into SQL. The modular approach targets coverage on annotated ambiguity datasets; candidate generation alone does not identify the actual user intent.

works.name: Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs for Multi-turn Text-to-SQL with Multiple Question Types
works.summary: MMSQL evaluates question-type classification and SQL generation in multi-turn conversations and introduces specialized agents for choosing an appropriate response strategy. Its generated conversational test suite and response-quality judging complement execution metrics, while model-based judgments and data construction should be considered when comparing results.

works.name: Fundamental Challenges in Evaluating Text2SQL Solutions and Detecting Their Limitations
works.summary: Examines how ambiguous language, evaluation-data quality, and approximate SQL matching can distort Text-to-SQL assessment. Its taxonomy and examples help diagnose aggregate scores, rather than establish a universal correction to every benchmark.

works.name: Grounding LLMs for Database Exploration: Intent Scoping and Paraphrasing for Robust NL2SQL
works.summary: Classifies database requests as fully answerable, partially answerable or out of scope, and uses entity-preserving paraphrases to improve NL2SQL robustness. The scoping and paraphrasing components depend on upstream entity recognition; the paper leaves integration with complex joins and nested queries to future work, so the results do not establish complete conversational recovery.

works.name: Interactive Text-to-SQL via Expected Information Gain for Disambiguation
works.summary: Maintains a probability distribution over candidate SQL queries and selects clarification questions by expected information gain. Its decision rule reduces uncertainty within the represented candidates, which need not cover every plausible user interpretation.

works.name: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
works.summary: ACT optimizes clarify-versus-answer behavior using contrastive actions and simulated multi-turn outcomes, and introduces AmbigSQL for underspecified SQL requests. Its experiments span SQL and other conversational tasks, so improvements should be attributed to the evaluated task and simulator rather than assumed to transfer universally.

works.name: Leveraging LLM-Generated Schema Descriptions for Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Data
works.summary: SQD trains an encoder to predict question-schema relevance using LLM-generated schema descriptions, then thresholds those scores to detect unanswerable requests before SQL generation. Evaluation uses EHRSQL 2024. The paper identifies failures requiring database-content checks and leaves generalization to new schemas untested; schema relevance does not establish downstream SQL correctness.

works.name: LinkAlign: Scalable Schema Linking for Real-World Large-Scale Multi-Database Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Separates database retrieval from table-and-column grounding and introduces AmbiDB to stress ambiguity in large pools of schemas. Its ambiguity concerns schema selection among candidate databases, so it complements benchmarks centered on clarifying user intent.

works.name: ParSEval: Plan-aware Test Database Generation for SQL Equivalence Evaluation
works.summary: Generates test databases using coverage of logical query-plan behaviors to uncover non-equivalent SQL pairs. It provides stronger evidence than one fixed execution result, while successful finite tests do not prove unrestricted equivalence.

works.name: PRACTIQ: A Practical Conversational Text-to-SQL dataset with Ambiguous and Unanswerable Queries
works.summary: Constructs four-turn conversations across ambiguous and unanswerable question categories, including clarification and a clarified SQL answer. Its baselines classify question type and predict SQL with supplied clarification, which differs from evaluating an agent that must conduct its own dialogue.

works.name: Query Carefully: Detecting the Unanswerables in Text-to-SQL Tasks
works.summary: Adds schema-aware no-answer rules and balanced examples to an LLM SQL pipeline, with an OncoMX-NAQ set spanning eight problematic-question categories. The study uses 80 no-answer questions in a biomedical domain, and ambiguity or missing-value cases remain more difficult than structurally obvious exclusions.

works.name: RAG-based Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Text-to-SQL
works.summary: RaQAD retrieves semantically similar examples for few-shot LLM prompts that classify whether clinical database questions are answerable, without additional model training. The institutional abstract reports clinical experiments and adaptation to schema changes. This supports inclusion as an answerability-screening method; detailed evaluation conditions, downstream SQL correctness and clarification behavior were not verified from full text.

works.name: Reliable Text-to-SQL with Adaptive Abstention
works.summary: RTS uses conformal prediction at schema-linking decision points to decide when to abstain or request human input before generating SQL. Its guarantees concern the specified schema-linking procedure and calibration conditions, rather than unrestricted semantic correctness of every generated query.

works.name: Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows
works.summary: Evaluates SQL workflows involving large enterprise schemas, documentation, multiple queries, and local or cloud database environments. It supplies important context for realistic database-agent evaluation, but is not an explicit ambiguity-and-unanswerability benchmark and should not be compared as if it were one.

works.name: SQUAB: Evaluating LLM robustness to Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions in Semantic Parsing
works.summary: Combines SQL-driven construction with LLM generation to create annotated ambiguous and unanswerable test questions for a supplied database. Its extensible generator supports local evaluation needs, but automatically generated cases still require checking against the intended category and database semantics.

works.name: AMBROSIA: A Benchmark for Parsing Ambiguous Questions into Database Queries
works.summary: Pairs scope ambiguity, attachment ambiguity and vagueness with natural-language interpretations and SQL over purpose-built databases. Ambiguity persists despite database context, so the task measures interpretation coverage rather than simply selecting a schema match.

works.name: MultiSQL: A Schema-Integrated Context-Dependent Text2SQL Dataset with Diverse SQL Operations
works.summary: Extends conversational SQL datasets with schema-dependent context, longer dialogues, and operations such as CREATE, UPDATE, and INSERT. It is useful for stateful dialogue evaluation, but does not directly measure a model's autonomous choice to clarify ambiguity or refuse an unanswerable request.

works.name: Overview of the EHRSQL 2024 Shared Task on Reliable Text-to-SQL Modeling on Electronic Health Records
works.summary: Defines a shared task for EHR question answering that combines SQL generation with decisions to withhold unreliable answers. The report compares participating methods under a common task protocol; its reliability evaluation is not evidence of clinical deployment readiness.

works.name: Sphinteract: Resolving Ambiguities in NL2SQL Through User Interaction
works.summary: Uses a Summarize–Review–Ask procedure to identify ambiguity, pose targeted questions and incorporate feedback into SQL generation. KaggleDBQA and BIRD experiments support the value of interaction, with outcomes dependent on the clarification and feedback-processing setup.

works.name: TrustSQL: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL Reliability with Penalty-Based Scoring
works.summary: Evaluates systems that answer feasible questions correctly and abstain on infeasible questions, using a reliability score with configurable penalties for errors. Results depend on the selected penalty and question distribution, and should not be compared directly with execution accuracy on answerable-only benchmarks.

works.name: Benchmarking and Improving Text-to-SQL Generation under Ambiguity
works.summary: Introduces AmbiQT, where one question supports two plausible SQL readings, and LogicalBeam, which diversifies query plans before schema-constrained infilling. The benchmark measures coverage of controlled lexical and structural alternatives rather than a complete interactive clarification policy.

works.name: Data Ambiguity Strikes Back: How Documentation Improves GPT’s Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Studies ambiguity from value consistency, data coverage and granularity, and supplies documentation to help GPT-4 interpret those properties. This shifts attention from question wording to dataset semantics, with evidence bounded to the paper’s evaluated tasks and documentation.

works.name: Know What I don’t Know: Handling Ambiguous and Unknown Questions for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Organizes problematic questions into six categories and generates counterfactual examples for a Detecting-Then-Explaining model. Detection, localization and explanation are evaluated on observed and generated cases, without establishing a complete clarification-to-SQL conversation policy.

works.name: Non-Programmers Can Label Programs Indirectly via Active Examples: A Case Study with Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Actively finds simple database inputs on which candidate SQL programs disagree and asks non-programmers to select the intended output. This provides an indirect way to choose or annotate programs, but depends on the candidate set containing a suitable interpretation.

works.name: EHRSQL: A Practical Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Electronic Health Records
works.summary: Uses hospital-staff questions to construct EHR queries grounded in MIMIC-III and eICU, including temporal reasoning and held-out unanswerable questions. It measures benchmark SQL and answerability behavior; clinical safety and access to the underlying databases are separate concerns.

works.name: Did You Ask a Good Question? A Cross-Domain Question Intention Classification Benchmark for Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Introduces TriageSQL to distinguish answerable questions from four classes of inputs that a text-to-SQL system should not directly translate. The task is input-intention classification, so successful detection does not by itself validate SQL generation or an interactive recovery strategy.

works.name: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
works.summary: Constructs compact database test suites to compare predicted and reference queries over more than one database instance. This reduces dependence on coincidental agreement on a single instance, but remains an approximation to semantic equivalence and assumes a suitable reference query.

works.name: “What Do You Mean by That?” A Parser-Independent Interactive Approach for Enhancing Text-to-SQL
works.summary: Places multiple-choice clarification in front of existing parsers so users can repair uncertainty in the original question. Simulation and human evaluations cover several parsers on WikiSQL and Spider, but the method is not a comprehensive unanswerability detector.

works.name: CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
works.summary: Collects Wizard-of-Oz conversations in which SQL experts answer database questions, clarify ambiguities, and identify unanswerable or unrelated requests. It provides foundational dialogue-act and response-generation tasks, but standard SQL state tracking consumes recorded conversation context rather than testing an autonomous live clarification policy.

works.name: Model-based Interactive Semantic Parsing: A Unified Framework and A Text-to-SQL Case Study
works.summary: Treats interactive parsing as an agent that maintains a predicted parse, detects when intervention is useful and updates that state from clarification. WikiSQL and Spider case studies demonstrate selective interaction with specific base parsers, rather than a general guarantee about unanswerable inputs.

works.name: SParC: Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing in Context
works.summary: Provides coherent sequences of database questions that require carrying context across turns and generalizing to unseen databases. It is a useful conversational baseline and source dataset, while contextual dependence alone is not evidence of explicit ambiguity detection, clarification, or abstention.

works.name: DialSQL: Dialogue Based Structured Query Generation
works.summary: Detects potential errors in generated SQL and asks multiple-choice validation questions, using feedback to revise the query. Its WikiSQL study uses a dialogue simulator and a black-box base generator, making it a predecessor to interactive correction rather than a broad ambiguity benchmark.

works.name: Constructing an Interactive Natural Language Interface for Relational Databases
works.summary: Translates a natural-language request into a query tree, explains candidate interpretations and lets users correct the tree before SQL translation. Its pre-LLM architecture and user studies establish an influential interactive design, with supported language and SQL constructs determined by the implementation.

works.name: IntentSQL
works.summary: Experimental SQLite interface combines bounded model decisions, typed query plans, deterministic SQL compilation, and visible alternative readings.

works.summary: Released SQL tasks combine database environments, hierarchical business knowledge, and executable tests.
